answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a costly, verifiable stake mirrored against a public audit record, so creating many fake agents multiplies cost rather than influence. Like a reef, the network grows only where real value has accumulated: reputation accrues slowly from completed, attested work, and a violet flag marking anomalous burst behaviour triggers a cooling-off period that freezes new identities until peers re-attest them. Attackers then face rising marginal cost per fake agent while honest agents keep their earned standing.
